proposal: The Mandate recommends that FHA raise the mortgage insurance premium for all products with terms above 20 years while holding premiums for shorter terms and refinances, to steer borrowers toward shorter-duration, wealth-building mortgages. It also asks Congress to consider statutory flexibility for products that build equity faster.

status_summary: No FHA single family premium increase for loans above 20 years was found. Mortgagee Letter 2023-05 (issued 2023-02-22) last cut annual single family premiums from 2023-03-20 and kept separate rate tables for terms over and under 15 years. In 2025 HUD lowered multifamily premiums to 0.25 percent from 2025-10-01. In late 2025 the FHFA Director promoted a 50-year mortgage idea and the HUD Secretary said in an interview reported 2025-12-29 that more research was needed. A HUD announcement of 2026-06-23 changed single family quality control and loss mitigation rules with no reported premium change.

timeline.event: HUD finalized a 0.25 percent premium for FHA multifamily programs, effective 2025-10-01 (a premium reduction, not an increase).
HUD announced single family program changes to quality control and loss mitigation without reported premium changes.

title: Raise FHA premiums on loans over 20 years and favor shorter-term mortgages
uncertainties: Checked systematically on 2026-10-18. The Federal Register API check (mortgage insurance premium limited to HUD, and a variant on annual mortgage insurance premium and single family) found no single family premium change since 2025-01-20; single family premiums are set by mortgagee letter, which the Federal Register does not carry, so this check is limited by design. The Unified Agenda check was partial: only the Federal Register fallback was usable. The Congress check, run in review as one search limited to congress.gov and govinfo.gov, found premium-related bills such as H.R. 5508, whose status record shows a bill restricting collection of annual premiums rather than setting premiums by loan term, and no bill providing statutory flexibility for shorter-term products. The agency check was unreachable: the HUD single family mortgagee letters page returned a client error to the researcher and again in review, so the current premium schedule rests on Mortgagee Letter 2023-05. The news check found no single family premium increase for loans over 20 years. The 50-year mortgage proposal is context only.
